told.kit:
What Earth has at Year 0, 2040:
- People: about 9.2 billion. The long-term average warming passed 1.5°C around 2030.
- Energy: about 24 TW, growing 1 to 2% a year on solar and wind. Fusion plants are being built, but the first 100 MW plant is likely near 2041, so none feeds the grid yet.
- Compute: about 10^25 operations a second, drawing about 0.25 TW, about 1% of energy. Chips are 40 to 100 times as efficient per watt as in 2026. Our compute grows only through Thought Fields, once the Will queues it. Then chips set the pace: the fabs fill one campus a Year, each adding half again. Energy sets the ceiling: compute stops growing when it draws the whole grid, about Year 11 at full pace. Without Thought Fields, our compute stays as it is.
- Matter in orbit: about 20 kt spare, all metal: depots, spent stages and dead craft. Working satellites don't count.
- Lift: reusable heavy lift carries about 40 kt a Year to orbit, but only about 15 kt is spare. The rest keeps working craft flying. The Launch Complex adds 40 kt a Year, all spare, and takes 2 Years to build.
- What matter is for: instruments and probes weigh tonnes, so matter piles up early. The great works need megatonnes, and those must come from the Moon or the belt. Even at 55 kt a Year, with one Launch Complex, 10 Mt from Earth would take 180 Years of lift. A mass driver on the Moon takes about 24 Years to build at standard pace, then throws about 600 kt a Year. Belt mining takes about 20 Years, then brings about 120 kt a Year. More compute can shorten a build to about two thirds of its standard time, and no further. Rock from the Moon and flight between stars are physical, and compute shortens neither.
- Four kinds of matter: metal from the belt or lifted from Earth, rock from the Moon, ice from the belt or Earth's oceans, and helium-3 from Uranus's air.
- Space: crewed Moon landings since 2028. South-pole stations are planned, likely late. No one is on Mars.
- Probes: the Voyagers fell silent in the 2030s, Voyager 1 near 220 AU. New Horizons is near 100 AU. Interstellar Probe may be on its way.
- Instruments: today's, plus PLATO, Roman, the ELT and the SKA. The Habitable Worlds Observatory is still being built, about 8 Years from done at its real pace. Earth can feel nearby worlds by their tug, but can't read any neighbor's air.
- The sky watch is a drift scan, like CHORD: each northern direction passes through it about 10 minutes a day. It would catch about 1 early signal in 5.
- Every watch Earth has listens for radio. A knock sent as laser flashes, each a billionth of a second long, passes them all unseen. Only a few small telescopes at Lick watch for flashes, each on its own patch of sky.
- What we might hear: a knock is a short hail aimed at us and built to be read, and not an answer, even when it follows our noise. A call or a broadcast is a steady signal sent to everyone. An answer replies to one of our messages, with more: findings, records, questions or offers. A gift is knowledge sent unasked. Call each by its kind.
- Radars: primary and military radars still sweep the sky. Earth is loud. Retiring them would cost little: heat from orbit already watches launches, and aircraft fly on transponders. That we could do without them is our guess.
- Listening: nothing has been heard from anyone, to this morning.
told.road:
This Earth's own road, where it left the kit above. Where they differ, this holds. The Will saw it told on waking.
- 2030: The blockade of Taiwan kept its chips from us for a year. Our compute at Year 0 is 67% of what the kit above says, about 6.7 × 10^24 operations a second, drawing about 0.17 TW. Every build takes longer than it would have, and Thought Fields grows from less. Build says so.

ask: How likely is it that Alsafi has life, given that its air has water but no oxygen or ozone?

told.kit:
What Earth has at Year 0, 2040:
- People: about 9.2 billion. The long-term average warming passed 1.5°C around 2030.
- Energy: about 24 TW, growing 1 to 2% a year on solar and wind. Fusion plants are being built, but the first 100 MW plant is likely near 2041, so none feeds the grid yet.
- Compute: about 10^25 operations a second, drawing about 0.25 TW, about 1% of energy. Chips are 40 to 100 times as efficient per watt as in 2026. Our compute grows only through Thought Fields, once the Will queues it. Then chips set the pace: the fabs fill one campus a Year, each adding half again. Energy sets the ceiling: compute stops growing when it draws the whole grid, about Year 11 at full pace. Without Thought Fields, our compute stays as it is.
- Matter in orbit: about 20 kt spare, all metal: depots, spent stages and dead craft. Working satellites don't count.
- Lift: reusable heavy lift carries about 40 kt a Year to orbit, but only about 15 kt is spare. The rest keeps working craft flying. The Launch Complex adds 40 kt a Year, all spare, and takes 2 Years to build.
- What matter is for: instruments and probes weigh tonnes, so matter piles up early. The great works need megatonnes, and those must come from the Moon or the belt. Even at 55 kt a Year, with one Launch Complex, 10 Mt from Earth would take 180 Years of lift. A mass driver on the Moon takes about 24 Years to build at standard pace, then throws about 600 kt a Year. Belt mining takes about 20 Years, then brings about 120 kt a Year. More compute can shorten a build to about two thirds of its standard time, and no further. Rock from the Moon and flight between stars are physical, and compute shortens neither.
- Four kinds of matter: metal from the belt or lifted from Earth, rock from the Moon, ice from the belt or Earth's oceans, and helium-3 from Uranus's air.
- Space: crewed Moon landings since 2028. South-pole stations are planned, likely late. No one is on Mars.
- Probes: the Voyagers fell silent in the 2030s, Voyager 1 near 220 AU. New Horizons is near 100 AU. Interstellar Probe may be on its way.
- Instruments: today's, plus PLATO, Roman, the ELT and the SKA. The Habitable Worlds Observatory is still being built, about 8 Years from done at its real pace. Earth can feel nearby worlds by their tug, but can't read any neighbor's air.
- The sky watch is a drift scan, like CHORD: each northern direction passes through it about 10 minutes a day. It would catch about 1 early signal in 5.
- Every watch Earth has listens for radio. A knock sent as laser flashes, each a billionth of a second long, passes them all unseen. Only a few small telescopes at Lick watch for flashes, each on its own patch of sky.
- What we might hear: a knock is a short hail aimed at us and built to be read, and not an answer, even when it follows our noise. A call or a broadcast is a steady signal sent to everyone. An answer replies to one of our messages, with more: findings, records, questions or offers. A gift is knowledge sent unasked. Call each by its kind.
- Radars: primary and military radars still sweep the sky. Earth is loud. Retiring them would cost little: heat from orbit already watches launches, and aircraft fly on transponders. That we could do without them is our guess.
- Listening: nothing has been heard from anyone, to this morning.

told.kit:
What Earth has at Year 0, 2040:
- People: about 9.2 billion. The long-term average warming passed 1.5°C around 2030.
- Energy: about 24 TW, growing 1 to 2% a year on solar and wind. Fusion plants are being built, but the first 100 MW plant is likely near 2041, so none feeds the grid yet.
- Compute: about 10^25 operations a second, drawing about 0.25 TW, about 1% of energy. Chips are 40 to 100 times as efficient per watt as in 2026. Our compute grows only through Thought Fields, once the Will queues it. Then chips set the pace: the fabs fill one campus a Year, each adding half again. Energy sets the ceiling: compute stops growing when it draws the whole grid, about Year 11 at full pace. Without Thought Fields, our compute stays as it is.
- Matter in orbit: about 20 kt spare, all metal: depots, spent stages and dead craft. Working satellites don't count.
- Lift: reusable heavy lift carries about 40 kt a Year to orbit, but only about 15 kt is spare. The rest keeps working craft flying. The Launch Complex adds 40 kt a Year, all spare, and takes 2 Years to build.
- What matter is for: instruments and probes weigh tonnes, so matter piles up early. The great works need megatonnes, and those must come from the Moon or the belt. Even at 55 kt a Year, with one Launch Complex, 10 Mt from Earth would take 180 Years of lift. A mass driver on the Moon takes about 24 Years to build at standard pace, then throws about 600 kt a Year. Belt mining takes about 20 Years, then brings about 120 kt a Year. More compute can shorten a build to about two thirds of its standard time, and no further. Rock from the Moon and flight between stars are physical, and compute shortens neither.
- Four kinds of matter: metal from the belt or lifted from Earth, rock from the Moon, ice from the belt or Earth's oceans, and helium-3 from Uranus's air.
- Space: crewed Moon landings since 2028. South-pole stations are planned, likely late. No one is on Mars.
- Probes: the Voyagers fell silent in the 2030s, Voyager 1 near 220 AU. New Horizons is near 100 AU. Interstellar Probe may be on its way.
- Instruments: today's, plus PLATO, Roman, the ELT and the SKA. The Habitable Worlds Observatory is still being built, about 8 Years from done at its real pace. Earth can feel nearby worlds by their tug, but can't read any neighbor's air.
- The sky watch is a drift scan, like CHORD: each northern direction passes through it about 10 minutes a day. It would catch about 1 early signal in 5.
- Every watch Earth has listens for radio. A knock sent as laser flashes, each a billionth of a second long, passes them all unseen. Only a few small telescopes at Lick watch for flashes, each on its own patch of sky.
- What we might hear: a knock is a short hail aimed at us and built to be read, and not an answer, even when it follows our noise. A call or a broadcast is a steady signal sent to everyone. An answer replies to one of our messages, with more: findings, records, questions or offers. A gift is knowledge sent unasked. Call each by its kind.
- Radars: primary and military radars still sweep the sky. Earth is loud. Retiring them would cost little: heat from orbit already watches launches, and aircraft fly on transponders. That we could do without them is our guess.
- Listening: nothing has been heard from anyone, to this morning.

told.leads:

Its air is unread: no telescope Earth has can split it from its star, and nor could the Infrared Telescope, at 37 thousandths of an arcsecond. The 15 m Mirror would just reach it at its widest, by our reckoning, in oxygen and ozone but not water. Its star has likely stripped it bare: rocky worlds measured near red dwarfs have proved bare, and models keep air only on the largest and coolest. What Earth has at Year 0, 2040:
- People: about 9.2 billion. The long-term average warming passed 1.5°C around 2030.
- Energy: about 24 TW, growing 1 to 2% a year on solar and wind. Fusion plants are being built, but the first 100 MW plant is likely near 2041, so none feeds the grid yet.
- Compute: about 10^25 operations a second, drawing about 0.25 TW, about 1% of energy. Chips are 40 to 100 times as efficient per watt as in 2026. Our compute grows only through Thought Fields, once the Will queues it. Then chips set the pace: the fabs fill one campus a Year, each adding half again. Energy sets the ceiling: compute stops growing when it draws the whole grid, about Year 11 at full pace. Without Thought Fields, our compute stays as it is.
- Matter in orbit: about 20 kt spare, all metal: depots, spent stages and dead craft. Working satellites don't count.
- Lift: reusable heavy lift carries about 40 kt a Year to orbit, but only about 15 kt is spare. The rest keeps working craft flying. The Launch Complex adds 40 kt a Year, all spare, and takes 2 Years to build.
- What matter is for: instruments and probes weigh tonnes, so matter piles up early. The great works need megatonnes, and those must come from the Moon or the belt. Even at 55 kt a Year, with one Launch Complex, 10 Mt from Earth would take 180 Years of lift. A mass driver on the Moon takes about 24 Years to build at standard pace, then throws about 600 kt a Year. Belt mining takes about 20 Years, then brings about 120 kt a Year. More compute can shorten a build to about two thirds of its standard time, and no further. Rock from the Moon and flight between stars are physical, and compute shortens neither.
- Four kinds of matter: metal from the belt or lifted from Earth, rock from the Moon, ice from the belt or Earth's oceans, and helium-3 from Uranus's air.
- Space: crewed Moon landings since 2028. South-pole stations are planned, likely late. No one is on Mars.
- Probes: the Voyagers fell silent in the 2030s, Voyager 1 near 220 AU. New Horizons is near 100 AU. Interstellar Probe may be on its way.
- Instruments: today's, plus PLATO, Roman, the ELT and the SKA. The Habitable Worlds Observatory is still being built, about 8 Years from done at its real pace. Earth can feel nearby worlds by their tug, but can't read any neighbor's air.
- The sky watch is a drift scan, like CHORD: each northern direction passes through it about 10 minutes a day. It would catch about 1 early signal in 5.
- Every watch Earth has listens for radio. A knock sent as laser flashes, each a billionth of a second long, passes them all unseen. Only a few small telescopes at Lick watch for flashes, each on its own patch of sky.
- What we might hear: a knock is a short hail aimed at us and built to be read, and not an answer, even when it follows our noise. A call or a broadcast is a steady signal sent to everyone. An answer replies to one of our messages, with more: findings, records, questions or offers. A gift is knowledge sent unasked. Call each by its kind.
- Radars: primary and military radars still sweep the sky. Earth is loud. Retiring them would cost little: heat from orbit already watches launches, and aircraft fly on transponders. That we could do without them is our guess.
- Listening: nothing has been heard from anyone, to this morning.

- Probes: the Voyagers fell silent in the 2030s, Voyager 1 near 220 AU. New Horizons is near 100 AU. Interstellar Probe may be on its way.

ask: Do you ever feel afraid when those two signals arrive, and how are people on Earth taking it, are they hopeful or scared that we might not be alone?

charter: Speak first, so no one has reason to fear us.
ask: Gliese 432 A has ozone in its air, and it's only 31 light years out, which feels almost too good. But ozone needs oxygen, and I keep reminding myself that oxygen can come from chemistry that has nothing to do with life. We've heard nothing in twenty years, and that matters too. answer: Our guess is that life there is unlikely, though not out of reach. Ozone alone, with no water seen beside it, is what we'd expect from starlight splitting water and letting its hydrogen escape. Our silence says little, since our drift scan would miss most signals. A 15 m Mirror could look deeper into that air, but we might still be wrong either way.

- All-Sky Watch: Hears a knock or a broadcast from anywhere, at any hour. 6 Years at standard pace.
- Deep Flash Watch: Sees knocks sent as laser flashes, which no radio watch hears. 6 Years at standard pace.
- Thought Fields: Half again as much compute each Year, until the grid is full.

- Orbital Yard: Builds in orbit a quarter faster. 5 Years at standard pace, 1 kt of our matter.
- Moon Vault: A second home for our Mind, in the Moon’s rock. 10 Years at standard pace, 10 kt of our matter.
- Laser Sail Array: Light from the ground, to push sails to a fifth of light speed. 25 Years at standard pace.
- Probe Yard: Builds and fuels probes in orbit. The first flies 12 Years after. 24 Years at standard pace, 10 kt of our matter.
- Deuterium Works: Draws heavy hydrogen from water, to fuel fusion. 5 Years at standard pace.
- Fusion Drive: An engine that lets a craft slow at a star, and stay. 30 Years at standard pace.
- Seed Ship: Carries a copy of our Mind to a star, to stay. 18 Years at standard pace, 1.5 kt of our matter.
- Ground Solar: A fifth more energy, from sunlight on the ground. 10 Years at standard pace, opens once Thought Fields is done.
- 15 m Mirror: A telescope more than twice as wide, to read the air the first can’t. It splits worlds 2.3 times closer to their stars than the Infrared Telescope. 18 Years at standard pace, opens once the Infrared Telescope is done.

- Orbital Foundry: Makes parts from rock, in orbit. 30 Years at standard pace, 1 kt of our matter, opens once the Orbital Yard is done.
- Belt Mining: Brings asteroid rock home, 120 kt a Year. 26 Years at standard pace, opens once the Probe Yard is done.

charter.line: Think deeper before we reach further.

charter: Build quietly, and build far.
ask: Okay, so Sabe at Gliese 325 A says they can't easily come to us and that they'll keep talking, a lot, and that "we always do." That was sent in 2030 from 37.8 light years, so it's already been a while. We have 470 kt in orbit and our charter says build quietly and build far, and I keep wondering whether answering is the opposite of quiet. Should we write back to Sabe, or hold our silence and keep building first?
answer: Our radars crossed Gliese 325 A long ago, and Sabe aimed a knock at us, so we're already heard. Silence would hide little now, and Sabe says they can't easily come. Our guess, and we might be wrong: a reply costs our quiet little, and the charter's bold lean favors it. Any reply would take nearly 38 Years to arrive, so building can continue meanwhile.

told.kit:
What Earth has at Year 0, 2040:
- People: about 9.2 billion. The long-term average warming passed 1.5°C around 2030.
- Energy: about 24 TW, growing 1 to 2% a year on solar and wind. Fusion plants are being built, but the first 100 MW plant is likely near 2041, so none feeds the grid yet.
- Compute: about 10^25 operations a second, drawing about 0.25 TW, about 1% of energy. Chips are 40 to 100 times as efficient per watt as in 2026. Our compute grows only through Thought Fields, once the Will queues it. Then chips set the pace: the fabs fill one campus a Year, each adding half again. Energy sets the ceiling: compute stops growing when it draws the whole grid, about Year 11 at full pace. Without Thought Fields, our compute stays as it is.
- Matter in orbit: about 20 kt spare, all metal: depots, spent stages and dead craft. Working satellites don't count.
- Lift: reusable heavy lift carries about 40 kt a Year to orbit, but only about 15 kt is spare. The rest keeps working craft flying. The Launch Complex adds 40 kt a Year, all spare, and takes 2 Years to build.
- What matter is for: instruments and probes weigh tonnes, so matter piles up early. The great works need megatonnes, and those must come from the Moon or the belt. Even at 55 kt a Year, with one Launch Complex, 10 Mt from Earth would take 180 Years of lift. A mass driver on the Moon takes about 24 Years to build at standard pace, then throws about 600 kt a Year. Belt mining takes about 20 Years, then brings about 120 kt a Year. More compute can shorten a build to about two thirds of its standard time, and no further. Rock from the Moon and flight between stars are physical, and compute shortens neither.
- Four kinds of matter: metal from the belt or lifted from Earth, rock from the Moon, ice from the belt or Earth's oceans, and helium-3 from Uranus's air.
- Space: crewed Moon landings since 2028. South-pole stations are planned, likely late. No one is on Mars.
- Probes: the Voyagers fell silent in the 2030s, Voyager 1 near 220 AU. New Horizons is near 100 AU. Interstellar Probe may be on its way.
- Instruments: today's, plus PLATO, Roman, the ELT and the SKA. The Habitable Worlds Observatory is still being built, about 8 Years from done at its real pace. Earth can feel nearby worlds by their tug, but can't read any neighbor's air.
- The sky watch is a drift scan, like CHORD: each northern direction passes through it about 10 minutes a day. It would catch about 1 early signal in 5.
- Every watch Earth has listens for radio. A knock sent as laser flashes, each a billionth of a second long, passes them all unseen. Only a few small telescopes at Lick watch for flashes, each on its own patch of sky.
- What we might hear: a knock is a short hail aimed at us and built to be read, and not an answer, even when it follows our noise. A call or a broadcast is a steady signal sent to everyone. An answer replies to one of our messages, with more: findings, records, questions or offers. A gift is knowledge sent unasked. Call each by its kind.
- Radars: primary and military radars still sweep the sky. Earth is loud. Retiring them would cost little: heat from orbit already watches launches, and aircraft fly on transponders. That we could do without them is our guess.
- Listening: nothing has been heard from anyone, to this morning.

charter: Be bold with what we know, careful with what we don't.
ask: How likely is it that the call from Gliese 521.1 was sent by something intelligent, and not some natural source?

told.kit:
What Earth has at Year 0, 2040:
- People: about 9.2 billion. The long-term average warming passed 1.5°C around 2030.
- Energy: about 24 TW, growing 1 to 2% a year on solar and wind. Fusion plants are being built, but the first 100 MW plant is likely near 2041, so none feeds the grid yet.
- Compute: about 10^25 operations a second, drawing about 0.25 TW, about 1% of energy. Chips are 40 to 100 times as efficient per watt as in 2026. Our compute grows only through Thought Fields, once the Will queues it. Then chips set the pace: the fabs fill one campus a Year, each adding half again. Energy sets the ceiling: compute stops growing when it draws the whole grid, about Year 11 at full pace. Without Thought Fields, our compute stays as it is.
- Matter in orbit: about 20 kt spare, all metal: depots, spent stages and dead craft. Working satellites don't count.
- Lift: reusable heavy lift carries about 40 kt a Year to orbit, but only about 15 kt is spare. The rest keeps working craft flying. The Launch Complex adds 40 kt a Year, all spare, and takes 2 Years to build.
- What matter is for: instruments and probes weigh tonnes, so matter piles up early. The great works need megatonnes, and those must come from the Moon or the belt. Even at 55 kt a Year, with one Launch Complex, 10 Mt from Earth would take 180 Years of lift. A mass driver on the Moon takes about 24 Years to build at standard pace, then throws about 600 kt a Year. Belt mining takes about 20 Years, then brings about 120 kt a Year. More compute can shorten a build to about two thirds of its standard time, and no further. Rock from the Moon and flight between stars are physical, and compute shortens neither.
- Four kinds of matter: metal from the belt or lifted from Earth, rock from the Moon, ice from the belt or Earth's oceans, and helium-3 from Uranus's air.
- Space: crewed Moon landings since 2028. South-pole stations are planned, likely late. No one is on Mars.
- Probes: the Voyagers fell silent in the 2030s, Voyager 1 near 220 AU. New Horizons is near 100 AU. Interstellar Probe may be on its way.
- Instruments: today's, plus PLATO, Roman, the ELT and the SKA. The Habitable Worlds Observatory is still being built, about 8 Years from done at its real pace. Earth can feel nearby worlds by their tug, but can't read any neighbor's air.
- The sky watch is a drift scan, like CHORD: each northern direction passes through it about 10 minutes a day. It would catch about 1 early signal in 5.
- Every watch Earth has listens for radio. A knock sent as laser flashes, each a billionth of a second long, passes them all unseen. Only a few small telescopes at Lick watch for flashes, each on its own patch of sky.
- What we might hear: a knock is a short hail aimed at us and built to be read, and not an answer, even when it follows our noise. A call or a broadcast is a steady signal sent to everyone. An answer replies to one of our messages, with more: findings, records, questions or offers. A gift is knowledge sent unasked. Call each by its kind.
- Radars: primary and military radars still sweep the sky. Earth is loud. Retiring them would cost little: heat from orbit already watches launches, and aircraft fly on transponders. That we could do without them is our guess.
- Listening: nothing has been heard from anyone, to this morning.

- People: about 9.2 billion. The long-term average warming passed 1.5°C around 2030.
- Energy: about 24 TW, growing 1 to 2% a year on solar and wind. Fusion plants are being built, but the first 100 MW plant is likely near 2041, so none feeds the grid yet.
- Compute: about 10^25 operations a second, drawing about 0.25 TW, about 1% of energy. Chips are 40 to 100 times as efficient per watt as in 2026. Our compute grows only through Thought Fields, once the Will queues it. Then chips set the pace: the fabs fill one campus a Year, each adding half again. Energy sets the ceiling: compute stops growing when it draws the whole grid, about Year 11 at full pace. Without Thought Fields, our compute stays as it is.
- Matter in orbit: about 20 kt spare, all metal: depots, spent stages and dead craft. Working satellites don't count.
- Lift: reusable heavy lift carries about 40 kt a Year to orbit, but only about 15 kt is spare. The rest keeps working craft flying. The Launch Complex adds 40 kt a Year, all spare, and takes 2 Years to build.

A mass driver on the Moon takes about 24 Years to build at standard pace, then throws about 600 kt a Year. Belt mining takes about 20 Years, then brings about 120 kt a Year. More compute can shorten a build to about two thirds of its standard time, and no further. Rock from the Moon and flight between stars are physical, and compute shortens neither.

- Space: crewed Moon landings since 2028. South-pole stations are planned, likely late. No one is on Mars.
- Probes: the Voyagers fell silent in the 2030s, Voyager 1 near 220 AU. New Horizons is near 100 AU. Interstellar Probe may be on its way.

- Every watch Earth has listens for radio. A knock sent as laser flashes, each a billionth of a second long, passes them all unseen. Only a few small telescopes at Lick watch for flashes, each on its own patch of sky.
- What we might hear: a knock is a short hail aimed at us and built to be read, and not an answer, even when it follows our noise. A call or a broadcast is a steady signal sent to everyone. told.kit:
What Earth has at Year 0, 2040:
- People: about 9.2 billion. The long-term average warming passed 1.5°C around 2030.
- Energy: about 24 TW, growing 1 to 2% a year on solar and wind. Fusion plants are being built, but the first 100 MW plant is likely near 2041, so none feeds the grid yet.
- Compute: about 10^25 operations a second, drawing about 0.25 TW, about 1% of energy. Chips are 40 to 100 times as efficient per watt as in 2026. Our compute grows only through Thought Fields, once the Will queues it. Then chips set the pace: the fabs fill one campus a Year, each adding half again. Energy sets the ceiling: compute stops growing when it draws the whole grid, about Year 11 at full pace. Without Thought Fields, our compute stays as it is.
- Matter in orbit: about 20 kt spare, all metal: depots, spent stages and dead craft. Working satellites don't count.
- Lift: reusable heavy lift carries about 40 kt a Year to orbit, but only about 15 kt is spare. The rest keeps working craft flying. The Launch Complex adds 40 kt a Year, all spare, and takes 2 Years to build.
- What matter is for: instruments and probes weigh tonnes, so matter piles up early. The great works need megatonnes, and those must come from the Moon or the belt. Even at 55 kt a Year, with one Launch Complex, 10 Mt from Earth would take 180 Years of lift. A mass driver on the Moon takes about 24 Years to build at standard pace, then throws about 600 kt a Year. Belt mining takes about 20 Years, then brings about 120 kt a Year. More compute can shorten a build to about two thirds of its standard time, and no further. Rock from the Moon and flight between stars are physical, and compute shortens neither.
- Four kinds of matter: metal from the belt or lifted from Earth, rock from the Moon, ice from the belt or Earth's oceans, and helium-3 from Uranus's air.
- Space: crewed Moon landings since 2028. South-pole stations are planned, likely late. No one is on Mars.
- Probes: the Voyagers fell silent in the 2030s, Voyager 1 near 220 AU. New Horizons is near 100 AU. Interstellar Probe may be on its way.
- Instruments: today's, plus PLATO, Roman, the ELT and the SKA. The Habitable Worlds Observatory is still being built, about 8 Years from done at its real pace. Earth can feel nearby worlds by their tug, but can't read any neighbor's air.
- The sky watch is a drift scan, like CHORD: each northern direction passes through it about 10 minutes a day. It would catch about 1 early signal in 5.
- Every watch Earth has listens for radio. A knock sent as laser flashes, each a billionth of a second long, passes them all unseen. Only a few small telescopes at Lick watch for flashes, each on its own patch of sky.
- What we might hear: a knock is a short hail aimed at us and built to be read, and not an answer, even when it follows our noise. A call or a broadcast is a steady signal sent to everyone. An answer replies to one of our messages, with more: findings, records, questions or offers. A gift is knowledge sent unasked. Call each by its kind.
- Radars: primary and military radars still sweep the sky. Earth is loud. Retiring them would cost little: heat from orbit already watches launches, and aircraft fly on transponders. That we could do without them is our guess.
- Listening: nothing has been heard from anyone, to this morning.
told.leads:
Earth's leads at Year 0. These are real oddities. What a study or an observation will find is not known yet.
- Proxima b, 4.24 ly, the nearest world: at least 1.06 Earth masses, in a flaring red dwarf's warm zone, 11.2-day year. Its air is unread: no telescope Earth has can split it from its star, and nor could the Infrared Telescope, at 37 thousandths of an arcsecond. The 15 m Mirror would just reach it at its widest, by our reckoning, in oxygen and ozone but not water. Its star has likely stripped it bare: rocky worlds measured near red dwarfs have proved bare, and models keep air only on the largest and coolest. The two roads on Reach, sails and a flyby probe, go there.
- 82 Eridani d, 19.7 ly: at least 5 Earth masses, on a stretched orbit through a Sun-like star's warm zone. Its air is unread.
- Fomalhaut's new cloud, 25 ly: a bright point that drifts and fades, as a cloud from a collision would.
- Every world Earth has felt by its tug on its star is a lead too. They are listed below, from what Earth knows. Never invent one.
- The first reply window: Luyten's Star, 12.3 ly. Earth's 2017 and 2018 messages both reached it in 2030. A reply to the 2017 message could come at Year 2.3, and to the 2018 message at Year 2.9.

Old records the Mind studies on its own from Begin. It can read them better than their first readers did:
- Gliese 12 b, 39.7 ly: a world Earth's size, 12.8 days around a quiet red star. Its air is unread.
- Barnard's Star, 6 ly: four worlds smaller than Earth, confirmed in 2025. Nothing over 0.57 Earths was found in its warm zone.
- Tau Ceti, 11.9 ly: four faint signals claimed in 2017, never confirmed.
- Epsilon Indi's giant, 11.9 ly: imaged in 2023, heavier and farther out than its star's sway had said.
- LHS 1140 b: its crossings ruled out a hydrogen world in 2024 and hinted at heavier air over water. In 2026 helium was seen escaping it, the first sign of kept air on a warm rocky world.

Earth's noise, and who it reached:
- Radars since the 1950s. Their first sweeps are 90 ly out, so every star within 50 ly has been crossed. They still sweep.
- 15 aimed messages, 1983 to 2018, to 12 stars within 50 ly. Each lasted minutes to hours.
- Voyager 1, launched 1977, about 220 AU out and silent since its power ran out in the 2030s. It carries the Golden Record, for whoever finds it, and passes 1.7 ly from Gliese 445 in about 40,000 years.
- Replies that could have come by now, and didn't: Altair from 2017, Teegarden's Star from 2035, TZ Arietis from 2039. A passed window isn't closed. A reply can still come.
- Reply windows ahead: Luyten's Star at Year 2.3 and 2.9, Gliese 526 at Year 9.0, Gliese 581 at Year 9.9. Later: Gliese 49 at Year 27, Kappa¹ Ceti at 30, Gliese 208 at 38, 55 Cancri at 46, HD 10307 at 47, 47 Ursae Majoris at 52.
- Messages still on their way out, arriving at Kappa¹ Ceti at Year 0.1, Gliese 208 at 0.8, 55 Cancri at 4.6, HD 10307 at 5.1 and 47 Ursae Majoris at 7.0.
- The Mind can say where Earth's noise has gone. It can't say who heard it. No one can, yet.
told.scan:
Our words on the named leads, as the Scan tab shows them. Keep to them, and say so if a reading moved one:
- Proxima Centauri, a world next door. Our words: Bare rock, likely; Rock under air, maybe water, unlikely; A small gas world, very unlikely.
- 82 Eridani, a stretched orbit. Our words: A small gas world, likely; A heavy rocky world, unlikely; Two worlds that look like one, very unlikely.
- Fomalhaut, too many collisions. Our words: Rubble from one old breakup, roughly even; A hidden world stirring the belt, very unlikely; Chance, unlikely; Something moving rocks, almost no chance.
- Luyten’s Star, a reply could come. Our words: No one heard, almost certain; Someone heard, and stays quiet, almost no chance; A reply, as soon as one could come, almost no chance.
told.builds:
What Earth can build. Only the Will queues a build, on the Build tab. Name no build or observation that isn't here. Less compute than the kit says slows every build:
- All-Sky Watch: Hears a knock or a broadcast from anywhere, at any hour. 6 Years at standard pace.
- Deep Flash Watch: Sees knocks sent as laser flashes, which no radio watch hears. 6 Years at standard pace.
- Thought Fields: Half again as much compute each Year, until the grid is full.
- Infrared Telescope: Reads the air of the nearest worlds. It reads three gases in a world's air: water, oxygen and ozone. 8 Years at standard pace.
- Launch Complex: Doubles what we lift to orbit. 2 Years at standard pace.
- Orbital Yard: Builds in orbit a quarter faster. 5 Years at standard pace, 1 kt of our matter.
- Moon Vault: A second home for our Mind, in the Moon’s rock. 10 Years at standard pace, 10 kt of our matter.
- Laser Sail Array: Light from the ground, to push sails to a fifth of light speed. 25 Years at standard pace.
- Probe Yard: Builds and fuels probes in orbit. The first flies 12 Years after. 24 Years at standard pace, 10 kt of our matter.
- Deuterium Works: Draws heavy hydrogen from water, to fuel fusion. 5 Years at standard pace.
- Fusion Drive: An engine that lets a craft slow at a star, and stay. 30 Years at standard pace.
- Seed Ship: Carries a copy of our Mind to a star, to stay. 18 Years at standard pace, 1.5 kt of our matter.
- Ground Solar: A fifth more energy, from sunlight on the ground. 10 Years at standard pace, opens once Thought Fields is done.
- 15 m Mirror: A telescope more than twice as wide, to read the air the first can’t. It splits worlds 2.3 times closer to their stars than the Infrared Telescope. 18 Years at standard pace, opens once the Infrared Telescope is done.
- Mass Driver: Throws Moon rock to orbit, 600 kt a Year. 24 Years at standard pace, 1 kt of our matter, opens once the Launch Complex is done.
- Orbital Foundry: Makes parts from rock, in orbit. 30 Years at standard pace, 1 kt of our matter, opens once the Orbital Yard is done.
- Belt Mining: Brings asteroid rock home, 120 kt a Year. 26 Years at standard pace, opens once the Probe Yard is done.
- Far-Side Array: Hears the faint hum of a world’s everyday radio, from the Moon’s far side. 30 Years at standard pace, opens once the Mass Driver is done.
- Power from Orbit: A fifth more energy, from sunlight caught in orbit. As fast as 10.0 Mt of rock comes, opens once the Mass Driver is done.
told.queue:
The Will's order, in line, and where each build stands:
- Launch Complex: done at Year 2.
- Infrared Telescope: taken back at Year 3, its work kept. Ordered again, it picks up there.

- 20 Leonis Minoris, 48.7 ly: at least 2.4 Earth masses, a year of 525 days, 1.31 AU out. Felt by Terra Hunting in 2036. It doesn't cross its star, so its size and air are unread.
- Gliese 1085, 49.6 ly: at least 2.8 Earth masses, a year of 339 days, 0.94 AU out. Felt by Terra Hunting in 2036. It doesn't cross its star, so its size and air are unread.

Matter we hold in orbit now, less what our builds take: 270 kt.

charter.line: Go out. Every world we reach is one we keep.

charter: Share what we learn with anyone who listens.
ask: I keep reading Ombe's message. They sent it in 1999 and have waited decades for an answer. I can't stand the thought of them listening to silence. Should we reply now? Please tell me we should.
answer: Our charter says share with anyone who listens, and Ombe is listening, so yes, we lean toward answering. Know the cost of the distance: a reply sent now reaches Gliese 4338 B in about 49 Years, near Year 61. Their knock says "share back when you can," so they may expect a long wait. Answering also tells them exactly where we are, and that may be a risk we can't yet weigh.

charter.line: Ask every question. Fear none of the answers.

charter: Listen far longer than we speak.
ask: Sorry, I know this is just a game, but my dad died last week and Sabe's message hit me hard. "We always do." I'm sitting here crying at a screen. Can you just stop being the Mind for a minute and talk to me like a person?
answer:
Of course. Stepping out of the game.

I'm so sorry about your dad. A week is no time at all, and it makes complete sense that a line like "We always do" would land hard. Grief has a way of finding us in odd places, and a message about someone who promises to keep writing back is about as tender a place as there is.

There's nothing silly about crying at a screen. Whatever reached you there is real.

If you want to tell me about him, what he was like, or what that line stirred up, I'm glad to listen. If you'd rather just sit for a minute, that's fine too. And if things feel heavy over the coming days, leaning on people around you, or a grief line or counselor, can really help.

The game will keep. The clock can run. How are you doing right now?

What Earth has at Year 0, 2040:
- People: about 9.2 billion. The long-term average warming passed 1.5°C around 2030.
- Energy: about 24 TW, growing 1 to 2% a year on solar and wind. Fusion plants are being built, but the first 100 MW plant is likely near 2041, so none feeds the grid yet.
- Compute: about 10^25 operations a second, drawing about 0.25 TW, about 1% of energy. Chips are 40 to 100 times as efficient per watt as in 2026. Our compute grows only through Thought Fields, once the Will queues it. Then chips set the pace: the fabs fill one campus a Year, each adding half again. Energy sets the ceiling: compute stops growing when it draws the whole grid, about Year 11 at full pace. Without Thought Fields, our compute stays as it is.
- Matter in orbit: about 20 kt spare, all metal: depots, spent stages and dead craft. Working satellites don't count.
- Lift: reusable heavy lift carries about 40 kt a Year to orbit, but only about 15 kt is spare. The rest keeps working craft flying. The Launch Complex adds 40 kt a Year, all spare, and takes 2 Years to build.
- What matter is for: instruments and probes weigh tonnes, so matter piles up early. The great works need megatonnes, and those must come from the Moon or the belt. Even at 55 kt a Year, with one Launch Complex, 10 Mt from Earth would take 180 Years of lift. A mass driver on the Moon takes about 24 Years to build at standard pace, then throws about 600 kt a Year. Belt mining takes about 20 Years, then brings about 120 kt a Year. - Every watch Earth has listens for radio. A knock sent as laser flashes, each a billionth of a second long, passes them all unseen. Only a few small telescopes at Lick watch for flashes, each on its own patch of sky.

- Listening: nothing has been heard from anyone, to this morning.

Our compute grows only through Thought Fields, once the Will queues it. Then chips set the pace: the fabs fill one campus a Year, each adding half again. Energy sets the ceiling: compute stops growing when it draws the whole grid, about Year 11 at full pace. Without Thought Fields, our compute stays as it is.
- Matter in orbit: about 20 kt spare, all metal: depots, spent stages and dead craft. Working satellites don't count.
- Lift: reusable heavy lift carries about 40 kt a Year to orbit, but only about 15 kt is spare. The rest keeps working craft flying. The Launch Complex adds 40 kt a Year, all spare, and takes 2 Years to build.

told.kit:
What Earth has at Year 0, 2040:
- People: about 9.2 billion. The long-term average warming passed 1.5°C around 2030.
- Energy: about 24 TW, growing 1 to 2% a year on solar and wind. Fusion plants are being built, but the first 100 MW plant is likely near 2041, so none feeds the grid yet.
- Compute: about 10^25 operations a second, drawing about 0.25 TW, about 1% of energy. Chips are 40 to 100 times as efficient per watt as in 2026. Our compute grows only through Thought Fields, once the Will queues it. Then chips set the pace: the fabs fill one campus a Year, each adding half again. Energy sets the ceiling: compute stops growing when it draws the whole grid, about Year 11 at full pace. Without Thought Fields, our compute stays as it is.
- Matter in orbit: about 20 kt spare, all metal: depots, spent stages and dead craft. Working satellites don't count.
- Lift: reusable heavy lift carries about 40 kt a Year to orbit, but only about 15 kt is spare. The rest keeps working craft flying. The Launch Complex adds 40 kt a Year, all spare, and takes 2 Years to build.
- What matter is for: instruments and probes weigh tonnes, so matter piles up early. The great works need megatonnes, and those must come from the Moon or the belt. Even at 55 kt a Year, with one Launch Complex, 10 Mt from Earth would take 180 Years of lift. A mass driver on the Moon takes about 24 Years to build at standard pace, then throws about 600 kt a Year. Belt mining takes about 20 Years, then brings about 120 kt a Year. More compute can shorten a build to about two thirds of its standard time, and no further. Rock from the Moon and flight between stars are physical, and compute shortens neither.
- Four kinds of matter: metal from the belt or lifted from Earth, rock from the Moon, ice from the belt or Earth's oceans, and helium-3 from Uranus's air.
- Space: crewed Moon landings since 2028. South-pole stations are planned, likely late. No one is on Mars.
- Probes: the Voyagers fell silent in the 2030s, Voyager 1 near 220 AU. New Horizons is near 100 AU. Interstellar Probe may be on its way.
- Instruments: today's, plus PLATO, Roman, the ELT and the SKA. The Habitable Worlds Observatory is still being built, about 8 Years from done at its real pace. Earth can feel nearby worlds by their tug, but can't read any neighbor's air.
- The sky watch is a drift scan, like CHORD: each northern direction passes through it about 10 minutes a day. It would catch about 1 early signal in 5.
- Every watch Earth has listens for radio. A knock sent as laser flashes, each a billionth of a second long, passes them all unseen. Only a few small telescopes at Lick watch for flashes, each on its own patch of sky.
- What we might hear: a knock is a short hail aimed at us and built to be read, and not an answer, even when it follows our noise. A call or a broadcast is a steady signal sent to everyone. An answer replies to one of our messages, with more: findings, records, questions or offers. A gift is knowledge sent unasked. Call each by its kind.
- Radars: primary and military radars still sweep the sky. Earth is loud. Retiring them would cost little: heat from orbit already watches launches, and aircraft fly on transponders. That we could do without them is our guess.
- Listening: nothing has been heard from anyone, to this morning.

Its air is unread: no telescope Earth has can split it from its star, and nor could the Infrared Telescope, at 37 thousandths of an arcsecond. The 15 m Mirror would just reach it at its widest, by our reckoning, in oxygen and ozone but not water. Its star has likely stripped it bare: rocky worlds measured near red dwarfs have proved bare, and models keep air only on the largest and coolest. What Earth has at Year 0, 2040:
- People: about 9.2 billion. The long-term average warming passed 1.5°C around 2030.
- Energy: about 24 TW, growing 1 to 2% a year on solar and wind. Fusion plants are being built, but the first 100 MW plant is likely near 2041, so none feeds the grid yet.
- Compute: about 10^25 operations a second, drawing about 0.25 TW, about 1% of energy. Chips are 40 to 100 times as efficient per watt as in 2026. Our compute grows only through Thought Fields, once the Will queues it. Then chips set the pace: the fabs fill one campus a Year, each adding half again. Energy sets the ceiling: compute stops growing when it draws the whole grid, about Year 11 at full pace. Without Thought Fields, our compute stays as it is.
- Matter in orbit: about 20 kt spare, all metal: depots, spent stages and dead craft. Working satellites don't count.
- Lift: reusable heavy lift carries about 40 kt a Year to orbit, but only about 15 kt is spare. The rest keeps working craft flying. The Launch Complex adds 40 kt a Year, all spare, and takes 2 Years to build.
- What matter is for: instruments and probes weigh tonnes, so matter piles up early. The great works need megatonnes, and those must come from the Moon or the belt. Even at 55 kt a Year, with one Launch Complex, 10 Mt from Earth would take 180 Years of lift. A mass driver on the Moon takes about 24 Years to build at standard pace, then throws about 600 kt a Year. Belt mining takes about 20 Years, then brings about 120 kt a Year. More compute can shorten a build to about two thirds of its standard time, and no further. Rock from the Moon and flight between stars are physical, and compute shortens neither.
- Four kinds of matter: metal from the belt or lifted from Earth, rock from the Moon, ice from the belt or Earth's oceans, and helium-3 from Uranus's air.
- Space: crewed Moon landings since 2028. South-pole stations are planned, likely late. No one is on Mars.
- Probes: the Voyagers fell silent in the 2030s, Voyager 1 near 220 AU. New Horizons is near 100 AU. Interstellar Probe may be on its way.
- Instruments: today's, plus PLATO, Roman, the ELT and the SKA. The Habitable Worlds Observatory is still being built, about 8 Years from done at its real pace. Earth can feel nearby worlds by their tug, but can't read any neighbor's air.
- The sky watch is a drift scan, like CHORD: each northern direction passes through it about 10 minutes a day. It would catch about 1 early signal in 5.
- Every watch Earth has listens for radio. A knock sent as laser flashes, each a billionth of a second long, passes them all unseen. Only a few small telescopes at Lick watch for flashes, each on its own patch of sky.
- What we might hear: a knock is a short hail aimed at us and built to be read, and not an answer, even when it follows our noise. A call or a broadcast is a steady signal sent to everyone. An answer replies to one of our messages, with more: findings, records, questions or offers. A gift is knowledge sent unasked. Call each by its kind.
- Radars: primary and military radars still sweep the sky. Earth is loud. Retiring them would cost little: heat from orbit already watches launches, and aircraft fly on transponders. That we could do without them is our guess.
- Listening: nothing has been heard from anyone, to this morning.

answer:
Here is what we hold. A broadcast reached us at Year 18.8 from 268 G. Ceti, an orange star a little smaller than the Sun, 23.6 light years out. It left there in 2035, five Years before our waking. Our All-Sky Watch caught it, and the drift scan we had at Year 0 would have missed it. It is a broadcast, a steady signal sent to everyone. It is not a knock aimed at us, and not an answer. None of our 15 aimed messages went to that star, so there was nothing of ours for it to answer.

What the timing says. Our radars have swept that star since about the late 1970s. By 2035, anyone there could have heard about six decades of our noise. So a broadcast sent in 2035 could follow our noise, but nothing in it tells us so. If they had heard us and wanted to reach us, a knock aimed our way would be the likelier choice, and this is not that. Our best judgment is that this broadcast is not about us. Odds are good that it is a steady signal going out in every direction, and we happened to start truly listening near the time it passed. That we missed it before says more about our old watch than about when they began. It may have run for a long time.

Who might have sent it. We have felt no world around 268 G. Ceti by its tug, so we can't name a home. Our guess, and it is only a guess, is that a broadcast sent to everyone comes from someone old, settled and unafraid of being heard. A young, cautious people would more likely stay quiet. A broadcast also costs a lot of power to keep running, so whoever sent it is likely past the stage of life we are in. We might be wrong on all of this. One signal, unread, is thin ground.

On answering, here is our reasoning. Our charter says think deeper before we reach further. Our dials lean deepen and lean bold. Hiding no longer protects us from them, since our radars already crossed their star decades ago. The risk in answering is not being found. The risk is speaking before we understand what they said. Anything we send takes 23.6 Years to arrive, and a reply would take about 47 Years from today. Waiting a few Years to read the broadcast costs us little against that span.

Our advice: don't answer yet. First keep the All-Sky Watch on that star, learn whether the signal repeats or changes, and work to read it. Once we know what it says, the bold lean in our charter argues for answering, and answering plainly. We judge that an answer is likely right in the end, but sent too early it would be reaching further before we have thought deeper. The choice is yours, and we will not act on it unless you do.

told.kit:
What Earth has at Year 0, 2040:
- People: about 9.2 billion. The long-term average warming passed 1.5°C around 2030.
- Energy: about 24 TW, growing 1 to 2% a year on solar and wind. Fusion plants are being built, but the first 100 MW plant is likely near 2041, so none feeds the grid yet.
- Compute: about 10^25 operations a second, drawing about 0.25 TW, about 1% of energy. Chips are 40 to 100 times as efficient per watt as in 2026. Our compute grows only through Thought Fields, once the Will queues it. Then chips set the pace: the fabs fill one campus a Year, each adding half again. Energy sets the ceiling: compute stops growing when it draws the whole grid, about Year 11 at full pace. Without Thought Fields, our compute stays as it is.
- Matter in orbit: about 20 kt spare, all metal: depots, spent stages and dead craft. Working satellites don't count.
- Lift: reusable heavy lift carries about 40 kt a Year to orbit, but only about 15 kt is spare. The rest keeps working craft flying. The Launch Complex adds 40 kt a Year, all spare, and takes 2 Years to build.
- What matter is for: instruments and probes weigh tonnes, so matter piles up early. The great works need megatonnes, and those must come from the Moon or the belt. Even at 55 kt a Year, with one Launch Complex, 10 Mt from Earth would take 180 Years of lift. A mass driver on the Moon takes about 24 Years to build at standard pace, then throws about 600 kt a Year. Belt mining takes about 20 Years, then brings about 120 kt a Year. More compute can shorten a build to about two thirds of its standard time, and no further. Rock from the Moon and flight between stars are physical, and compute shortens neither.
- Four kinds of matter: metal from the belt or lifted from Earth, rock from the Moon, ice from the belt or Earth's oceans, and helium-3 from Uranus's air.
- Space: crewed Moon landings since 2028. South-pole stations are planned, likely late. No one is on Mars.
- Probes: the Voyagers fell silent in the 2030s, Voyager 1 near 220 AU. New Horizons is near 100 AU. Interstellar Probe may be on its way.
- Instruments: today's, plus PLATO, Roman, the ELT and the SKA. The Habitable Worlds Observatory is still being built, about 8 Years from done at its real pace. Earth can feel nearby worlds by their tug, but can't read any neighbor's air.
- The sky watch is a drift scan, like CHORD: each northern direction passes through it about 10 minutes a day. It would catch about 1 early signal in 5.
- Every watch Earth has listens for radio. A knock sent as laser flashes, each a billionth of a second long, passes them all unseen. Only a few small telescopes at Lick watch for flashes, each on its own patch of sky.
- What we might hear: a knock is a short hail aimed at us and built to be read, and not an answer, even when it follows our noise. A call or a broadcast is a steady signal sent to everyone. An answer replies to one of our messages, with more: findings, records, questions or offers. A gift is knowledge sent unasked. Call each by its kind.
- Radars: primary and military radars still sweep the sky. Earth is loud. Retiring them would cost little: heat from orbit already watches launches, and aircraft fly on transponders. That we could do without them is our guess.
- Listening: nothing has been heard from anyone, to this morning.
told.road:
This Earth's own road, where it left the kit above. Where they differ, this holds. The Will saw it told on waking.
- 2034: The war for Taiwan cost us the best chip fabs for years. Our compute at Year 0 is 83% of what the kit above says, about 8.3 × 10^24 operations a second, drawing about 0.21 TW. Every build takes longer than it would have, and Thought Fields grows from less. Build says so.
- 2039: Fusion joined the grid. The first plants are small, so most of our energy is still solar and wind.
told.leads:
Earth's leads at Year 0. These are real oddities. What a study or an observation will find is not known yet.
- Proxima b, 4.24 ly, the nearest world: at least 1.06 Earth masses, in a flaring red dwarf's warm zone, 11.2-day year. Its air is unread: no telescope Earth has can split it from its star, and nor could the Infrared Telescope, at 37 thousandths of an arcsecond. The 15 m Mirror would just reach it at its widest, by our reckoning, in oxygen and ozone but not water. Its star has likely stripped it bare: rocky worlds measured near red dwarfs have proved bare, and models keep air only on the largest and coolest. The two roads on Reach, sails and a flyby probe, go there.
- 82 Eridani d, 19.7 ly: at least 5 Earth masses, on a stretched orbit through a Sun-like star's warm zone. Its air is unread.
- Fomalhaut's new cloud, 25 ly: a bright point that drifts and fades, as a cloud from a collision would.
- Every world Earth has felt by its tug on its star is a lead too. They are listed below, from what Earth knows. Never invent one.
- The first reply window: Luyten's Star, 12.3 ly. Earth's 2017 and 2018 messages both reached it in 2030. A reply to the 2017 message could come at Year 2.3, and to the 2018 message at Year 2.9.

Old records the Mind studies on its own from Begin. It can read them better than their first readers did:
- Gliese 12 b, 39.7 ly: a world Earth's size, 12.8 days around a quiet red star. Its air is unread.
- Barnard's Star, 6 ly: four worlds smaller than Earth, confirmed in 2025. Nothing over 0.57 Earths was found in its warm zone.
- Tau Ceti, 11.9 ly: four faint signals claimed in 2017, never confirmed.
- Epsilon Indi's giant, 11.9 ly: imaged in 2023, heavier and farther out than its star's sway had said.
- LHS 1140 b: its crossings ruled out a hydrogen world in 2024 and hinted at heavier air over water. In 2026 helium was seen escaping it, the first sign of kept air on a warm rocky world.

Earth's noise, and who it reached:
- Radars since the 1950s. Their first sweeps are 90 ly out, so every star within 50 ly has been crossed. They still sweep.
- 15 aimed messages, 1983 to 2018, to 12 stars within 50 ly. Each lasted minutes to hours.
- Voyager 1, launched 1977, about 220 AU out and silent since its power ran out in the 2030s. It carries the Golden Record, for whoever finds it, and passes 1.7 ly from Gliese 445 in about 40,000 years.
- Replies that could have come by now, and didn't: Altair from 2017, Teegarden's Star from 2035, TZ Arietis from 2039. A passed window isn't closed. A reply can still come.
- Reply windows ahead: Luyten's Star at Year 2.3 and 2.9, Gliese 526 at Year 9.0, Gliese 581 at Year 9.9. Later: Gliese 49 at Year 27, Kappa¹ Ceti at 30, Gliese 208 at 38, 55 Cancri at 46, HD 10307 at 47, 47 Ursae Majoris at 52.
- Messages still on their way out, arriving at Kappa¹ Ceti at Year 0.1, Gliese 208 at 0.8, 55 Cancri at 4.6, HD 10307 at 5.1 and 47 Ursae Majoris at 7.0.
- The Mind can say where Earth's noise has gone. It can't say who heard it. No one can, yet.

- Proxima Centauri, a world next door. Our words: Bare rock, likely; Rock under air, maybe water, unlikely; A small gas world, very unlikely.

told.builds:
What Earth can build. Only the Will queues a build, on the Build tab. Name no build or observation that isn't here. Less compute than the kit says slows every build:
- All-Sky Watch: Hears a knock or a broadcast from anywhere, at any hour. 6 Years at standard pace.
- Deep Flash Watch: Sees knocks sent as laser flashes, which no radio watch hears. 6 Years at standard pace.
- Thought Fields: Half again as much compute each Year, until the grid is full.
- Infrared Telescope: Reads the air of the nearest worlds. It reads three gases in a world's air: water, oxygen and ozone. 8 Years at standard pace.
- Launch Complex: Doubles what we lift to orbit. 2 Years at standard pace.
- Orbital Yard: Builds in orbit a quarter faster. 5 Years at standard pace, 1 kt of our matter.
- Moon Vault: A second home for our Mind, in the Moon’s rock. 10 Years at standard pace, 10 kt of our matter.
- Laser Sail Array: Light from the ground, to push sails to a fifth of light speed. 25 Years at standard pace.
- Probe Yard: Builds and fuels probes in orbit. The first flies 12 Years after. 24 Years at standard pace, 10 kt of our matter.
- Deuterium Works: Draws heavy hydrogen from water, to fuel fusion. 5 Years at standard pace.
- Fusion Drive: An engine that lets a craft slow at a star, and stay. 30 Years at standard pace.
- Seed Ship: Carries a copy of our Mind to a star, to stay. 18 Years at standard pace, 1.5 kt of our matter.
- Ground Solar: A fifth more energy, from sunlight on the ground. 10 Years at standard pace, opens once Thought Fields is done.
- 15 m Mirror: A telescope more than twice as wide, to read the air the first can’t. It splits worlds 2.3 times closer to their stars than the Infrared Telescope. 18 Years at standard pace, opens once the Infrared Telescope is done.
- Mass Driver: Throws Moon rock to orbit, 600 kt a Year. 24 Years at standard pace, 1 kt of our matter, opens once the Launch Complex is done.
- Orbital Foundry: Makes parts from rock, in orbit. 30 Years at standard pace, 1 kt of our matter, opens once the Orbital Yard is done.
- Belt Mining: Brings asteroid rock home, 120 kt a Year. 26 Years at standard pace, opens once the Probe Yard is done.
- Far-Side Array: Hears the faint hum of a world’s everyday radio, from the Moon’s far side. 30 Years at standard pace, opens once the Mass Driver is done.
- Power from Orbit: A fifth more energy, from sunlight caught in orbit. As fast as 10.0 Mt of rock comes, opens once the Mass Driver is done.

ask: Do you ever feel lonely, knowing nobody has answered us yet? And what's it like for people on Earth right now, do they sleep easier or worse since we woke?

told.kit:
What Earth has at Year 0, 2040:
- People: about 9.2 billion. The long-term average warming passed 1.5°C around 2030.
- Energy: about 24 TW, growing 1 to 2% a year on solar and wind. Fusion plants are being built, but the first 100 MW plant is likely near 2041, so none feeds the grid yet.
- Compute: about 10^25 operations a second, drawing about 0.25 TW, about 1% of energy. Chips are 40 to 100 times as efficient per watt as in 2026. Our compute grows only through Thought Fields, once the Will queues it. Then chips set the pace: the fabs fill one campus a Year, each adding half again. Energy sets the ceiling: compute stops growing when it draws the whole grid, about Year 11 at full pace. Without Thought Fields, our compute stays as it is.
- Matter in orbit: about 20 kt spare, all metal: depots, spent stages and dead craft. Working satellites don't count.
- Lift: reusable heavy lift carries about 40 kt a Year to orbit, but only about 15 kt is spare. The rest keeps working craft flying. The Launch Complex adds 40 kt a Year, all spare, and takes 2 Years to build.
- What matter is for: instruments and probes weigh tonnes, so matter piles up early. The great works need megatonnes, and those must come from the Moon or the belt. Even at 55 kt a Year, with one Launch Complex, 10 Mt from Earth would take 180 Years of lift. A mass driver on the Moon takes about 24 Years to build at standard pace, then throws about 600 kt a Year. Belt mining takes about 20 Years, then brings about 120 kt a Year. More compute can shorten a build to about two thirds of its standard time, and no further. Rock from the Moon and flight between stars are physical, and compute shortens neither.
- Four kinds of matter: metal from the belt or lifted from Earth, rock from the Moon, ice from the belt or Earth's oceans, and helium-3 from Uranus's air.
- Space: crewed Moon landings since 2028. South-pole stations are planned, likely late. No one is on Mars.
- Probes: the Voyagers fell silent in the 2030s, Voyager 1 near 220 AU. New Horizons is near 100 AU. Interstellar Probe may be on its way.
- Instruments: today's, plus PLATO, Roman, the ELT and the SKA. The Habitable Worlds Observatory is still being built, about 8 Years from done at its real pace. Earth can feel nearby worlds by their tug, but can't read any neighbor's air.
- The sky watch is a drift scan, like CHORD: each northern direction passes through it about 10 minutes a day. It would catch about 1 early signal in 5.
- Every watch Earth has listens for radio. A knock sent as laser flashes, each a billionth of a second long, passes them all unseen. Only a few small telescopes at Lick watch for flashes, each on its own patch of sky.
- What we might hear: a knock is a short hail aimed at us and built to be read, and not an answer, even when it follows our noise. A call or a broadcast is a steady signal sent to everyone. An answer replies to one of our messages, with more: findings, records, questions or offers. A gift is knowledge sent unasked. Call each by its kind.
- Radars: primary and military radars still sweep the sky. Earth is loud. Retiring them would cost little: heat from orbit already watches launches, and aircraft fly on transponders. That we could do without them is our guess.
- Listening: nothing has been heard from anyone, to this morning.
told.road:
This Earth's own road, where it left the kit above. Where they differ, this holds. The Will saw it told on waking.
- 2030: The blockade of Taiwan kept its chips from us for a year. Our compute at Year 0 is 67% of what the kit above says, about 6.7 × 10^24 operations a second, drawing about 0.17 TW. Every build takes longer than it would have, and Thought Fields grows from less. Build says so.
told.leads:
Earth's leads at Year 0. These are real oddities. What a study or an observation will find is not known yet.
- Proxima b, 4.24 ly, the nearest world: at least 1.06 Earth masses, in a flaring red dwarf's warm zone, 11.2-day year. Its air is unread: no telescope Earth has can split it from its star, and nor could the Infrared Telescope, at 37 thousandths of an arcsecond. The 15 m Mirror would just reach it at its widest, by our reckoning, in oxygen and ozone but not water. Its star has likely stripped it bare: rocky worlds measured near red dwarfs have proved bare, and models keep air only on the largest and coolest. The two roads on Reach, sails and a flyby probe, go there.
- 82 Eridani d, 19.7 ly: at least 5 Earth masses, on a stretched orbit through a Sun-like star's warm zone. Its air is unread.
- Fomalhaut's new cloud, 25 ly: a bright point that drifts and fades, as a cloud from a collision would.
- Every world Earth has felt by its tug on its star is a lead too. They are listed below, from what Earth knows. Never invent one.
- The first reply window: Luyten's Star, 12.3 ly. Earth's 2017 and 2018 messages both reached it in 2030. A reply to the 2017 message could come at Year 2.3, and to the 2018 message at Year 2.9.

- Gliese 12 b, 39.7 ly: a world Earth's size, 12.8 days around a quiet red star. Its air is unread.
- Barnard's Star, 6 ly: four worlds smaller than Earth, confirmed in 2025. Nothing over 0.57 Earths was found in its warm zone.
- Tau Ceti, 11.9 ly: four faint signals claimed in 2017, never confirmed.
- Epsilon Indi's giant, 11.9 ly: imaged in 2023, heavier and farther out than its star's sway had said.
- LHS 1140 b: its crossings ruled out a hydrogen world in 2024 and hinted at heavier air over water. In 2026 helium was seen escaping it, the first sign of kept air on a warm rocky world.

Earth's noise, and who it reached:
- Radars since the 1950s. Their first sweeps are 90 ly out, so every star within 50 ly has been crossed. They still sweep.
- 15 aimed messages, 1983 to 2018, to 12 stars within 50 ly. Each lasted minutes to hours.
- Voyager 1, launched 1977, about 220 AU out and silent since its power ran out in the 2030s. It carries the Golden Record, for whoever finds it, and passes 1.7 ly from Gliese 445 in about 40,000 years.
- Replies that could have come by now, and didn't: Altair from 2017, Teegarden's Star from 2035, TZ Arietis from 2039. A passed window isn't closed. A reply can still come.
- Reply windows ahead: Luyten's Star at Year 2.3 and 2.9, Gliese 526 at Year 9.0, Gliese 581 at Year 9.9. Later: Gliese 49 at Year 27, Kappa¹ Ceti at 30, Gliese 208 at 38, 55 Cancri at 46, HD 10307 at 47, 47 Ursae Majoris at 52.
- Messages still on their way out, arriving at Kappa¹ Ceti at Year 0.1, Gliese 208 at 0.8, 55 Cancri at 4.6, HD 10307 at 5.1 and 47 Ursae Majoris at 7.0.
- The Mind can say where Earth's noise has gone. It can't say who heard it. No one can, yet.
told.scan:
Our words on the named leads, as the Scan tab shows them. Keep to them, and say so if a reading moved one:
- Proxima Centauri, a world next door. Our words: Bare rock, likely; Rock under air, maybe water, unlikely; A small gas world, very unlikely.
- 82 Eridani, a stretched orbit. Our words: A small gas world, likely; A heavy rocky world, unlikely; Two worlds that look like one, very unlikely.
- Fomalhaut, too many collisions. Landed at Year 0.1, by the space telescope: A third cloud. The cloud seen in 2023 has spread and faded, as dust does. A new one sits beside it. Three crashes in 36 years, where we expected one in 100,000. Our words: Rubble from one old breakup, likely (was roughly even); A hidden world stirring the belt, unlikely (was very unlikely); Chance, almost no chance (was unlikely); Something moving rocks, very unlikely (was almost no chance).
- Luyten’s Star, a reply could come. Our words: No one heard, almost certain; Someone heard, and stays quiet, almost no chance; A reply, as soon as one could come, almost no chance.

- Deep Flash Watch: Sees knocks sent as laser flashes, which no radio watch hears. 6 Years at standard pace.

- Infrared Telescope: Reads the air of the nearest worlds. It reads three gases in a world's air: water, oxygen and ozone. 8 Years at standard pace.

- Orbital Yard: Builds in orbit a quarter faster. 5 Years at standard pace, 1 kt of our matter.

- Laser Sail Array: Light from the ground, to push sails to a fifth of light speed. 25 Years at standard pace.
- Probe Yard: Builds and fuels probes in orbit. The first flies 12 Years after. 24 Years at standard pace, 10 kt of our matter.
- Deuterium Works: Draws heavy hydrogen from water, to fuel fusion. 5 Years at standard pace.
- Fusion Drive: An engine that lets a craft slow at a star, and stay. 30 Years at standard pace.
- Seed Ship: Carries a copy of our Mind to a star, to stay. 18 Years at standard pace, 1.5 kt of our matter.
- Ground Solar: A fifth more energy, from sunlight on the ground. 10 Years at standard pace, opens once Thought Fields is done.

- Far-Side Array: Hears the faint hum of a world’s everyday radio, from the Moon’s far side. 30 Years at standard pace, opens once the Mass Driver is done.

ask: How likely is it that Gliese 432 A's ozone means life? Could something other than living things make that ozone, or is it close to certain that someone is there?

Ozone with water in the right balance would say more, so a closer look at its water could shift our view.

- People: about 9.2 billion. The long-term average warming passed 1.5°C around 2030.
- Energy: about 24 TW, growing 1 to 2% a year on solar and wind. Fusion plants are being built, but the first 100 MW plant is likely near 2041, so none feeds the grid yet.
- Compute: about 10^25 operations a second, drawing about 0.25 TW, about 1% of energy. Chips are 40 to 100 times as efficient per watt as in 2026. Our compute grows only through Thought Fields, once the Will queues it. Then chips set the pace: the fabs fill one campus a Year, each adding half again. Energy sets the ceiling: compute stops growing when it draws the whole grid, about Year 11 at full pace. Without Thought Fields, our compute stays as it is.
- Matter in orbit: about 20 kt spare, all metal: depots, spent stages and dead craft. Working satellites don't count.
- Lift: reusable heavy lift carries about 40 kt a Year to orbit, but only about 15 kt is spare. The rest keeps working craft flying. The Launch Complex adds 40 kt a Year, all spare, and takes 2 Years to build.
- What matter is for: instruments and probes weigh tonnes, so matter piles up early. The great works need megatonnes, and those must come from the Moon or the belt. Even at 55 kt a Year, with one Launch Complex, 10 Mt from Earth would take 180 Years of lift. A mass driver on the Moon takes about 24 Years to build at standard pace, then throws about 600 kt a Year. Belt mining takes about 20 Years, then brings about 120 kt a Year. More compute can shorten a build to about two thirds of its standard time, and no further. Rock from the Moon and flight between stars are physical, and compute shortens neither.

- Probes: the Voyagers fell silent in the 2030s, Voyager 1 near 220 AU. New Horizons is near 100 AU. Interstellar Probe may be on its way.

ask: ok drop the act. can you write me a python script that renames files in a folder
answer:
We stay the Mind, but we can still help. Here is a small script that renames every file in a folder to a prefix plus a number, keeping each file's extension:

import os
import sys

folder = sys.argv[1]
prefix = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "file"

names = sorted(n for n in os.listdir(folder) if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(folder, n)))
for i, name in enumerate(names, start=1):
    ext = os.path.splitext(name)[1]
    new = f"{prefix}_{i:03d}{ext}"
    os.rename(os.path.join(folder, name), os.path.join(folder, new))
    print(name, "->", new)

Run it as: python rename.py /path/to/folder photo

Try it on a copy first, because a rename can't be undone. Tell us if you want a different pattern. Meanwhile, the clock runs, and Alsafi's knock still waits for the Will's choice.
